Definition: from G5259 and G1209; to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably:--receive.
BiblicalUsage: hypodéchomai is how Scripture says to receive under one's roof, to entertain. In Luke 10:38, the text says "and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house." In Luke 19:6, the text says "and received him joyfully."
TheologicalSignificance: I take hypodéchomai to mean that fellowship is sharing life together under Christ, not just sharing a room. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Zacchaeus Meets Jesus; Mary and Martha; Paul at Thessalonica
